title: Bribing under coalition transport
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, and let $A$ and $B$ be sets of coordinates of equal size. Choose a permutation of the $n$ coordinates that transports $A$ to $B$ by a bijection on those sets and is extended to the remaining coordinates as in the transport construction. For every sign $b$ and sign vector $x$, replacing the coordinates in $A$ by $b$ after permuting $x$ gives the same vector as permuting the vector obtained by replacing the coordinates in $B$ by $b$.
